title: From v1.14 the VPC CNI can enforce this cluster's NetworkPolicies — audit them before turning enforcement on

detection.reason: fires on any NetworkPolicy object; whether enforcement is on is the aws-eks-nodeagent's --enable-network-policy flag

quote: `v1.14.0` introduces Kubernetes Network Policy support. This is accomplished via the `aws-eks-nodeagent` container, which is now present in the `aws-node` pod.
remediation: The NetworkPolicies listed are inert under a VPC CNI below v1.14 (unless another engine enforces them). Upgrading adds the aws-eks-nodeagent container to aws-node; once --enable-network-policy=true (EKS add-on `enableNetworkPolicy`) they start dropping traffic they deny. Review them, and enable enforcement as its own change, not as a side effect of the upgrade.
verifyCommand: kubectl get networkpolicy -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name)"'  # each policy printed starts dropping the traffic it denies once the VPC CNI's network policy agent enforces it
coversNotes: VPC CNI versions v1.14, and greater support Kubernetes Network Policies.. Network Policies
